title: Freya and the Typewriter
premise: In 1938, nonbinary apprentice clockmaker Beatrix Whitlock is summoned to repair the observatory's failing master clock, where they meet Freya, the census taker whose questions begin to unravel Beatrix's carefully invisible life. As the town's authorities grow suspicious of Beatrix's refusal to fit the census's categories, Freya risks her own standing to shield them, and the two fall in love while racing to finish the clockwork before the workshop is seized. The climax comes when the inspector arrives mid-repair: Freya falsifies the records to declare Beatrix's workshop a protected civic instrument, trading her career for their safety. The clock strikes true at last, and Beatrix and Freya leave together, no longer invisible but finally seen by each other.
about_author: C. M. Delacroix is the pen name of a former horologist's apprentice turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing municipal records in coastal New England towns. Their fiction excavates the quiet lives hidden in ledgers, census forms, and clock towers.

chapters.title: The Question Too Many
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Summoned to the observatory, they climb the tower with their toolbox and their rule of invisibility, only to find census taker Freya Ashworth waiting with her forms. One question about household composition stops Beatrix cold. The beat is wary fascination: two people who both live by other people's categories, measuring each other.

chapters.title: Gears and Ledgers
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Beatrix works on the master clock by day while Freya returns, ostensibly to verify records, really to watch them work. They trade stories of the machines that govern their lives: gears, forms, ledgers. The inspector begins asking about the workshop's 'irregular' occupant. The beat is tenderness blooming under surveillance.

chapters.title: What the Census Cannot Hold
chapters.summary: Freya's POV. Ordered to report Beatrix's noncompliance, Freya discovers her supervisor has already marked the workshop for seizure. She burns her draft report and confesses everything to Beatrix in the clock room, where they admit their love among the turning gears. The beat is terror and relief intertwined, the choice made before it's spoken.

chapters.title: The Clock Strikes True
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The inspector arrives at dawn as the final wheel is set. Freya presents falsified papers designating the workshop a protected civic instrument, sacrificing her post. The clock strikes for the first time in months as the two walk out together past the stunned official. The beat is hard-won peace: seen at last, and free.
